plain_description.what: On a standard intent dataset (CLINC150) with the same embeddings, compares the label-free 'no matching cell' score from flat k-means cells with standard out-of-scope detectors. Two of these use class labels (nearest class centre, class Mahalanobis) and two do not (nearest-neighbour distance, one global ellipsoid). No judge calls.
plain_description.why: It checks whether the earlier 0.974 detection score is special to the cell approach or just reflects the embedding, by comparing with standard baselines.
plain_description.information: If simple detectors match it, the score belongs to the embedding; if the cells match labelled detectors without labels, that is a real advantage. Result: the k-means cells beat the two label-free baselines and are within 0.01 of the two labelled detectors, without using labels. The lead depends on the settings (nearest-neighbour with k=1 does slightly better). These are flat k-means cells, not the tree, on one dataset and one embedder.
